description: Check what a watch-face design (a `wff-watchface` catalog design) costs on a watch, with Google's own validators: the WFF schema, the memory footprint and the Watch Face Push checks a watch runs before it installs a face. Returns `passed` and one entry per check with its findings; each finding carries a `suggestion` saying what to change. The `memory-footprint` check's `memory` is the face's decoded size against `activeLimitBytes` and `ambientLimitBytes`, and its `contributors` list the resources that cost the most (pixel size, decoded bytes, the size each is drawn at). Keep both modes under their limits: downscale an image to the size it is drawn at, and give ambient a dim or reduced variant rather than the full-colour one. A bitmap the face names that the design does not pin fails `bundle-resources`; pin it with ui_builder_put_asset. This runs the full packager, so call it when an edit pass is done and before ui_builder_publish_watch_face, not after every edit; an unchanged face answers from cache. Between runs, every ui_builder_apply, ui_builder_replace_design_document and ui_builder_put_asset on a watch face already replies with `watchFaceCost`: a cheap estimate of the same budgets (`active` and `ambient` as `usedBytes`, `limitBytes`, `percentOfLimit`), the `topContributors` with what to do about each, and the estimate's `errors`; read it after each edit and fix what it flags before building further. A failing face is a report with `passed: false`, not an error. A host whose operator left Google's validators off answers `watch_face_validation_disabled`.

agentModel.description: Optional current model name shown to design viewers; self-reported. Omit when unknown.

agentName.description: Optional agent/client name shown to design viewers; self-reported.

revision.description: The revision to validate. Defaults to the current one.

token.description: A grant token from poll_access, when you cannot set the X-Compose-Preview-Token header yourself — an MCP client fixes its headers at connect time, so this is how a token approved during this session is used in it. Prefer the header where you control it.
